### The Version PR needs a PAT to trigger CI — and an unset secret hard-fails checkout

**Symptom** — The changesets "Version Packages" PR opened, but its CI and release checks sat in
`action_required` and never ran. Wiring a PAT reference into the release workflow to fix that turned
main red instead: `actions/checkout` failed with `Input required and not supplied: token`.

**Root cause** — Two linked traps. (1) GitHub deliberately doesn't trigger workflows on PRs authored by
the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` (anti-recursion), so a Version PR opened by the changesets action never
kicks off CI. (2) `actions/checkout`'s `token:` input, given the empty string a not-yet-created
`secrets.*` resolves to, errors out rather than falling back — so referencing a missing secret breaks
the whole workflow, including the publish path.

**Fix / rule** — Author the Version PR with a fine-grained PAT (repo-scoped, Contents + Pull requests:
read/write) on both the checkout `token:` and the changesets action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` env, so the PR
comes from a real user and CI runs automatically. Reference the secret defensively —
`${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT || github.token }}` — so an absent or expired PAT degrades to the built-in
token instead of hard-failing, and emit a `::warning::` when it's missing. The PAT is git/PR auth only;
npm publishing stays OIDC/token-free (`id-token: write` + trusted publishers). Fine-grained PATs expire
(≤ 1 year); the "RELEASE_PAT missing" warning in the release log is the rotation cue.

All green — the merge is clean, no revert needed. Now to your ask.

Here's the landscape. Two workflows post PR checks, and the trap is the **conditional** jobs:

| Workflow | Jobs | Conditional (skipped on some PRs) |
|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` | build, typecheck, test, lint, publint, attw, repository, commitlint, docs-changes, docs | `docs` (only if docs changed), `commitlint` (PR-only) |
| `changeset-check.yml` | detect-release-impact, require-changeset, docs-and-internal-only | `require-changeset` / `docs-and-internal-only` (mutually exclusive by release impact) |

The naive fix — list every check as "required" in branch protection — **breaks** on exactly those conditional jobs: a required check that gets skipped is never reported, so GitHub parks the PR at "Expected — waiting for status" forever. And the required list would need editing every time a job is added or renamed.

## Recommended approach: one gate job per workflow

Add a `ci-gate` job to `ci.yml` and a `changeset-gate` job to `changeset-check.yml`. Each `needs:` every other job in its workflow, runs with `if: always()`, and fails only if a dependency actually **failed or was cancelled** — treating *skipped* as fine. Then branch protection requires just those two gate checks.

Why this answers "regardless of which workflow":
- Each workflow carries its own gate; requiring both means a PR merges only when *both* workflows are fully resolved and green.
- The required-checks list is **two stable names** that never change as jobs come and go.
- Conditional/skipped jobs no longer block.
- `gh pr merge --auto` then genuinely waits, because there's a required check that stays pending until everything resolves.

The one alternative — requiring each check individually — I'd reject for the skip-trap and maintenance churn above.

This is two parts: a **workflow code change** (safe, reviewable) and a **branch-protection change** (admin, and consequential — a bad config blocks all merges). Order matters: land the gate jobs on main first, *then* require them, so no PR blocks waiting on a check that doesn't exist yet.

Before I touch anything, one decision:

`changeset-gate`. The audit found a solid base but real gaps: **0/12 GitHub Actions are
SHA-pinned** (mutable `@v1`/`@v7` tags, including three third-party actions — one running under
`contents:write` + `id-token:write` in the release job), **immutable releases is OFF**, **tags

requirement), and there's no Dependabot config, CodeQL, or least-privilege split in `docs.yml`.

Goal: lock down main, make releases tamper-proof (immutable + protected tags), and close the
supply-chain gaps — without ever deadlocking the solo-maintainer, bot-driven Version PR flow.

**Why the flow can't break (grounding facts, verified in code):**
- The changesets bot pushes `chore: version packages` to `changeset-release/main` and opens a PR;
  it never pushes to `main` directly. Main-scoped rules bite only at PR merge.
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` calls `gh release create <name>@<version>` — always a *new*
  unique tag/release, and `versionReleased()` skips ones that already exist. No tag moves, no
  deletes, no asset re-uploads, no release edits. So immutable releases + tag `non_fast_forward` +
  `deletion` never interfere.
- CI on the Version PR depends on `RELEASE_PAT` (already set); once we require PR + checks, that
  PAT is load-bearing — without it the PR's checks would park in `action_required` and deadlock.

**Confirmed choices:** squash-only merges · include CodeQL + harden-runner (audit) + required
signed commits · add repo admin (me) as a break-glass bypass actor on the main ruleset.

# Harden pantoken: protect main, immutable releases, supply-chain best practices

## Context

pantoken publishes many packages to npm. The release flow is automated (changesets → OIDC
trusted publishing with provenance) and just gained a branch ruleset requiring `ci-gate` /
`changeset-gate`. The audit found a solid base but real gaps: **0/12 GitHub Actions are
SHA-pinned** (mutable `@v1`/`@v7` tags, including three third-party actions — one running under
`contents:write` + `id-token:write` in the release job), **immutable releases is OFF**, **tags
are unprotected**, main protection is checks-only (no force-push/deletion block, no PR
requirement), and there's no Dependabot config, CodeQL, or least-privilege split in `docs.yml`.

Goal: lock down main, make releases tamper-proof (immutable + protected tags), and close the
supply-chain gaps — without ever deadlocking the solo-maintainer, bot-driven Version PR flow.

**Why the flow can't break (grounding facts, verified in code):**
- The changesets bot pushes `chore: version packages` to `changeset-release/main` and opens a PR;
  it never pushes to `main` directly. Main-scoped rules bite only at PR merge.
- `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` calls `gh release create <name>@<version>` — always a *new*
  unique tag/release, and `versionReleased()` skips ones that already exist. No tag moves, no
  deletes, no asset re-uploads, no release edits. So immutable releases + tag `non_fast_forward` +
  `deletion` never interfere.
- CI on the Version PR depends on `RELEASE_PAT` (already set); once we require PR + checks, that
  PAT is load-bearing — without it the PR's checks would park in `action_required` and deadlock.

**Confirmed choices:** squash-only merges · include CodeQL + harden-runner (audit) + required
signed commits · add repo admin (me) as a break-glass bypass actor on the main ruleset.

## Rollout order (each phase safe; nothing toggled mid-release)

Precondition: run while the release flow is at rest — main green, no open Version PR, no pending
files in `.changeset/`. Confirm `RELEASE_PAT` is present (`gh secret list`).

### Phase 1 — Repo settings (gh api, admin; no code)
1. Squash-only: `gh api repos/thedannywahl/pantoken -X PATCH -F allow_merge_commit=false -F allow_rebase_merge=false -F allow_squash_merge=true`
2. Hygiene: same PATCH with `delete_branch_on_merge=true`, `allow_update_branch=true`
